paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think Paul is getting at. Life in the family of faith is not a solo sport. When someone is caught in a trespass, the spiritual ones restore him with gentleness, and they keep an eye on themselves too (Galatians 6:1). Then Paul says, "Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ." (Galatians 6:2)

But carrying each other does not mean dodging your own work. Paul says each one should test his own work, and then adds that each one should carry his own load (Galatians 6:4-5). If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself (Galatians 6:3). So help the person next to you, and stay honest about your own batch. I have flipped over plenty of cookies I was bragging about, and the bottom told the truth every time.

Then Paul reminds us how sowing works: "God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return." (Galatians 6:7) Sow to please the Spirit, and the Spirit brings a harvest of eternal life (Galatians 6:8). So when you're tired of doing good, hang in there, because Paul says, "Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up." (Galatians 6:9) And do good to everyone you can, especially the family of faith (Galatians 6:10). That's how my ovens stay ready, one small good thing at a time.
